subject: Nanotechnology
title: Graphene Supercapacitors
description: A fast breakdown of Graphene Supercapacitors for builders.

hook.text: Charge in seconds, discharge in seconds — supercapacitors with graphene electrodes deliver instant power bursts.

buildup.text: Graphene's theoretical surface area is 2630 m² per gram — ions line up on both sides of every single-atom sheet.

discovery.text: Laser-scribed graphene creates porous 3D structures from graphite oxide — a simple, scalable process.

twist.text: Graphene sheets restack during processing — reducing the accessible surface and killing capacitance.

climax.text: Spacer nanoparticles between sheets prevent restacking — maintaining high surface area in practical devices.

punchline.text: A single-atom sheet stores energy on both sides — instant power from a carbon lattice.

quiz.question: Why is graphene ideal for supercapacitor electrodes?
options: It stores energy in chemical bonds like a battery
Its enormous surface area allows ions to line up on both sides of each atomic sheet
It generates electricity when exposed to light
